creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Muster runs as a bare binary out of `.build/arm64-apple-macosx/debug/`. There is no Dock icon, nothing to keep in the Dock, no double-click, no `open -a muster`, and no way to hand somebody a thing they can run. Every launch is a shell invocation from the repo.

It is also where the descriptor ceiling from a_28MLhxLsn actually bites. launchd hands a GUI-launched process a soft `RLIMIT_NOFILE` of 256 and a developer's shell reports millions, so the limit that matters only appears once there is a bundle to launch. The two want doing together.

SwiftPM has no bundle product, so `./dev` would grow a step that assembles `Contents/MacOS` and an `Info.plist` around the built binary. `app.setActivationPolicy(.regular)` is already set in Sources/muster/main.swift, so the app already behaves like a regular one once it is launched as one.

Open: whether the gate builds a bundle every time or only a release path does - the gate is meant to stay fast and nothing in it needs one.

Signing and notarization are a separate question and belong with going public rather than here. This is about being able to launch it like an app on the machine that built it.
title: 📦 Ship as an app bundle, not a binary in .build
